newsitem.title: CANADA: Weak gold price seen behind Kazakhstan mine move.
newsitem.headline: Weak gold price seen behind Kazakhstan mine move.

text.p: The current weakness in the gold price was probably the reason why the Kazakhstan government rejected a proposal by Teck Corp and First Dynasty Mines Ltd to develop the Vasilkovskoye gold deposit, Teck president Norman Keevil said on Monday.

Teck said late on Friday that the government decided not to accept the offer. Keevil declined to specify terms of the offer for 80 percent of the deposit, but he said the main issue appeared to be price. About three other groups had submitted competing offers, he said.
"It was a difficult decision for them. Our bid was the most attractive...but it boiled down to price," he said in an interview.
The government did not explain its decision. "But my guess is they will hold off on it (development of Vasilkovskoye) and reopen it when the gold price is higher," Keevil said.
"If the gold price went to $500, I think there would be some aggressive bidding," he said.
Keevil said a recent slide in the gold price did not affect the value of Teck's offer significantly since the basic terms were set in a package submitted in late September.

But the Kazakhstan government apparently decided the resource would be more valuable if it waited for better market conditions. Teck's offer also included a price participation mechanism tied to the gold price, but that was not a major component, Keevil said.
Keevil said the government did not give any indication whether it would invite proposals in the future for development of Vasilkovskoye, which has reserves of 14 million ounces of gold.
But Teck remains interested in reopening negotiations on the deposit if the opportunity arises.

The project has been embroiled in controversy. Kazakhstan bypassed a tender organized by the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development and awarded rights to Placer Dome Inc in 1995. Placer later pulled out and is still demanding the return of a US$35 million deposit.

Kazakhstan then organized a tender that resulted in a deal with Teck last summer. But that broke down over a dispute on a government-proposed investment plan. The government then re-invited Teck to bid in August.
On the Toronto Stock Exchange, Teck stock was down 0.35 at 29.50, while First Dynasty was unchanged at 3.45.
